authority_refs: Military Content, Roster, Recruitment, and Development Authority V1.0.1
Unit Definition and Card Authoring Standard V1.0.0

rules.title: Schema conformance
rules.test: Record must validate against Unit_Definition_Schema_V1.json.

rules.title: Stable ID verification
rules.test: Implementation-targeted records require a non-empty stable_unit_id and Registry evidence. Candidate examples are insufficient.

rules.title: Canonical path verification
rules.test: Any requested write requires a verified canonical_path owned by the current repository architecture.

rules.title: No active state
rules.test: Definition must not contain current personnel, location, commander assignment, morale, fatigue, ammunition, equipment fill, supply quantity, readiness, or current formation state.

rules.title: Realm ownership
rules.test: Realm eligibility must be explicit. Theater placement or cultural similarity must not grant cross-realm ownership.

rules.title: Roster slot
rules.test: Unit must point to an approved roster and family. A missing role cannot justify invention.

rules.title: Distinct gameplay value
rules.test: Unit must differ materially through recruitment, institution, region, equipment, training, role, campaign burden, politics, AI use, lineage, or opportunity cost.

rules.title: Recruitment source separation
rules.test: A building, culture value, population record, obligation, region, port, order, or equipment profile must not be treated as a recruited unit or complete recruitment pool.

rules.title: Equipment authority
rules.test: Exact equipment must reference an approved profile. Generic cultural aesthetics do not prove equipment.

rules.title: Formation boundary
rules.test: Formation eligibility may be defined, but runtime formation state and bespoke formation engines are prohibited.

rules.title: Conditional counterplay
rules.test: Anti-class roles must not claim immunity or deterministic victory. Strength depends on supported conditions and counterplay.

rules.title: Tactical values
rules.test: New or promoted tactical statistics require current scale ownership, comparator evidence, and applicable battle validation.

rules.title: Lineage substance
rules.test: Lineage must describe meaningful recruitment, equipment, training, role, availability, cost, regional, or institutional change. Rename-only lineage fails.

rules.title: Era and history
rules.test: Era scope constrains plausibility but must not automatically unlock, replace, or upgrade a unit. Historical outcomes cannot be mandatory.

rules.title: Late Era authorization
rules.test: Late Era production requires explicit authorization. Retained source references alone are insufficient.

rules.title: Historical classification
rules.test: Terminology, chronology, equipment, organization, and counterfactual claims require an explicit claim status and source references.

rules.title: Selective inheritance
rules.test: Imported mechanics or mod-derived ideas require a selective_inheritance_record. Source names and synopses are not proof and are not exhaustive limits.

rules.title: AI transparency
rules.test: AI guidance must include recruitment priorities, avoidance conditions, support, supply awareness, decisive reasons, and blockers. Hidden bonuses are prohibited.

rules.title: Full presentation card
rules.test: Description, availability, recruitment, lineage, cultural path, player use, historical flavor, visual brief, related units, and designer notes must be present or explicitly classified.

rules.title: Visual evidence boundary
rules.test: Visual notes or images must not prove ownership, equipment inventory, culture state, active availability, or tactical values.

rules.title: Legacy preservation
rules.test: Modernization must preserve or ledger legacy statistics, flavor, references, events, objectives, variants, AI notes, and visual notes.

rules.title: Duplicate comparison
rules.test: Same-name, same-role, same-realm, or same-lineage candidates require direct comparison before merge, split, deprecation, or replacement.

rules.title: Modern Medieval II acceptance
rules.test: Unit must have readable role, campaign consequence, faction value, strategic recruitment, strengths, weaknesses, credible counterplay, and manageable player workload.

rules.title: Implementation gate
rules.test: Production writes require approved roster, definition, ID, path, schema, Registry evidence, asset inventory, deterministic import plan, rollback, and authorization.

rules.title: Validation claim discipline
rules.test: Static checks cannot be labeled importer, compile, runtime, save/load, migration, replay, performance, balance, or battle validation.

modern_medieval_ii_acceptance_questions: Does the unit strengthen realm or regional identity?
Is the unit more than a cosmetic duplicate?
Is history emergent rather than forced?
Can AI explain use and avoidance?
Can the definition be represented as stable data?
Are selectively inherited elements adapted rather than copied wholesale?
